summary: Verdict: benign (confidence 0.85). F3 shows sign-ins concentrated from Portugal via university VPN edge device LT-3104. Rejected claims: impossible travel was a non-interactive mail-sync token; Turkcell ASN 193.140.10.21 is shared organizational egress with 201 accounts MFA-authenticating in 30 days; password-spray pattern is background noise across 54 accounts; both KEV-listed VPN appliances are either patched (vpn-edge-02) or not involved in this account's sign-ins (vpn-edge-01). No compromise signal survived critic review.

findings.claim: Most sign-ins come from PT (10 events)

rejected_claims.claim: Impossible travel: Manisa → Lisbon in 32 min
rejected_claims.reason: critic: premature impossible-travel claim: the TR event is a non-interactive mail-sync token (ExchangeSync/15), not the person; the PT sign-ins use university VPN vpn-edge-02 from device LT-3104

rejected_claims.claim: Suspicious sign-ins from an ASN outside the account's baseline: Turkcell (TR), 1 event(s)
rejected_claims.reason: critic: shared-egress ASN: 201 distinct accounts completed MFA from 193.140.10.21 in the last 30 days (threshold 10); this ASN is the organisation's own exit (shared NAT / mail relay), not a new personal network for the user

rejected_claims.claim: Password spray then success: 193.140.10.21 failed against 54 accounts (60 failures) and later signed in as this user
rejected_claims.reason: critic: 193.140.10.21 looks like shared egress: 201 distinct accounts completed MFA from this IP in the last 30 days (threshold 10); failures across many accounts are expected background noise, not a coordinated spray

rejected_claims.claim: VPN appliance vpn-edge-02 (firmware 22.7R2.8) runs a product listed in CISA KEV (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282, …)
rejected_claims.reason: critic: firmware 22.7R2.8 already includes the fixes for the KEV entries we can version-check (CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282)

rejected_claims.claim: VPN appliance vpn-edge-01 (firmware 22.7R2.3) runs a product listed in CISA KEV (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282, …)
rejected_claims.reason: critic: vpn-edge-01 did not carry a sign-in for prof.kaya@aegean.edu; its KEV status is not relevant to this account's exposure

actions.action: Confirm user travel and device ownership for LT-3104 and validate MFA/VPN logs for the 10 Portugal sign-ins.
Document firmware patch verification for vpn-edge-01 and vpn-edge-02 against CISA KEV CVEs (CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282).
Monitor shared egress IP 193.140.10.21 for MFA burst anomalies and establish per-user baseline thresholds.

risk.rationale: All suspicious signals for prof.kaya@aegean.edu were rejected with specific, verified criticisms: the TR event is a non-interactive ExchangeSync token (not the user), the PT sign-ins are university VPN (vpn-edge-02) from device LT-3104, the Turkcell/shared-egress IP 193.140.10.21 is the organisation's own NAT used by 201 accounts with MFA (above threshold 10), the login failures are background noise across many accounts not a spray, and the VPN KEV concerns are either patched in firmware 22.7R2.8 or irrelevant (vpn-edge-01 never signed into this account). The only verified finding F3 (PT sign-in clustering, LIKELY 0.5) is consistent with legitimate VPN use and is weak/explained. No confirmed account takeover chain, no exposure, no conflicting evidence.
